author: ojiudezue
title: Ship march v5.6.0→v5.7.2 (bathroom-exhaust ships; WS-A guest trust; Energy Saver Pre-Cool unification) + the AV-closet lesson: a dead actuator makes URA fail SILENTLY — check device availability FIRST, and the D1/D2/D3 triage (visibility ship / reconcile design / auto-reload parked on OC)
summary: Long arc closing entry 025's cycle and three more: v5.6.0 bathroom-exhaust + humidity unification SHIPPED+validated; v5.6.1-3 config-flow string fixes; v5.7.0 WS-A guest-detection trust (Tier 3, lost-but-away admitted to the away veto, path-alpha byte-identical); v5.7.1 Energy Saver Pre-Cool (Tier 3, PV-gated unification of weather pre-cool + solar banking, one known migration L3 FAIL tracked). Then the operationally-instructive tail: operator reported 'lighting automations broke after the fan changes' — code was byte-unchanged; real causes were (a) integrations offline and (b) in the AV closet, the room's Shelly light relay sitting unavailable/restored:true, so URA detected occupancy perfectly and its turn_on/turn_off no-op'd against a dead entity. The per-room unavailable-entities tracker read 0 the whole outage because it only watched INPUT sensors, never actuators. Shipped v5.7.2 (Tier 1): the sensor now covers actuators with structured per-entity detail (roles/category/state/reason/since; reason includes offline_since_restart from the restored placeholder). Live validation was stronger than planned: the flaky AV Shelly re-dropped post-restart and the sensor caught it exactly as designed.
decisions: SILENT-ACTUATOR FAILURE CLASS + TRIAGE ORDER — when a room 'stops automating', check the actuator device's availability BEFORE suspecting URA code or config. A URA room cannot actuate an unavailable entity; the failure is invisible because service calls no-op. Codified as a CLAUDE.md Troubleshooting section. Corollary: device offline ≠ integration failed — 47/48 Shelly config entries stayed 'loaded' while their devices sat off-WiFi; reloading a loaded entry only helps a device that is back on the network (proven live: reloads of Sonoff/Tuya/stuck-Shelly revived nothing off-WiFi).

D1 OVERLOAD, NOT A NEW SENSOR — extend the existing UnavailableEntitiesSensor rather than adding an entity: nothing internal consumed its count (verified), per-room entity count is already heavy, and the sensor/actuator distinction is better served by categorized attributes (unavailable_sensors vs unavailable_actuators + details[] with reason tokens). Operator explicitly asked for 'richer and more structured'; reason vocabulary: offline_since_restart / device_unreachable / entity_missing / state_unknown.

D2 STUDY-BEFORE-BUILD, LIVE-INTENT-ONLY — operator's instinct: 'a bad restore would be really difficult to troubleshoot; study what HA learned first.' Research confirmed: RestoreEntity is restart-only (async_added_to_hass), core has NO reconcile-on-reconnect primitive, and some devices power back to a default state. Design filed (PLANNING_reconcile_on_return.md): per-room ActuatorReconciler that resolves desired state from LIVE inputs (occupied/is_dark/sleep) — NEVER a stored snapshot; six guards (config-membership, manual_mode off, boot-settle, 15s debounce, 6/hr cap, coordinator data ready); lights+fans only, covers/climate excluded; Tier 2-DB.

D3 AUTO-RELOAD PARKED ON THE OC, NOT BUILT — operator: reloads tax the system, integration provenance uncertain (HA-native vs HACS, incl. deliberately-killed integrations), sketch a precision/performance safety pattern or discard. Parked as OC plan Appendix C: only viable as an Optimization-Coordinator action under the autonomy ladder (L1 Shadow first), per-entry targeted, provenance-allowlisted, recoverability-gated, single-shot-per-outage, rate-capped, kill-switched. Operator may discard if D1 visibility + a manual reload proves sufficient.

WS-A v5.7.0 (earlier in arc) — lost-but-away trackers admitted to the away veto via a guarded path-beta (indoor-clear + grace + sleep-exempt + debounce), path-alpha byte-identical; falsifiable invariant 'never AWAY while a resident is home' mutation-anchored across 6 behavioral tests. v5.7.1 — pre-cool unified under one PV-gated trigger with the PV check re-run EVERY cycle including re-engagement; solar banking retired via migration (one L3 FAIL: runtime-only banking-OFF not preserved when the legacy options key is absent — tracked, low-harm because pre-cool is PV-gated).
alternatives_considered: Blaming the fan/humidity cycles for the lighting breakage (operator's initial hypothesis). Disproven by byte-identical diff of the lighting functions across v5.6.0-v5.7.1 — regression checks should diff the suspect surface before archaeology.

My own mid-investigation wrong guess: 'AV closet is mis-wired to the grow controller for lux/motion.' The operator's config page + entity registry proved occupancy_lux_temp_humidity_avcloset IS the Zigbee multisensor. Lesson re-learned: verify device identity from the registry (IEEE/battery/linkquality) before claiming mis-wiring.
Blanket-reloading all 48 Shelly entries. Rejected: blinks every working light for near-zero gain; only 1 entry was actually setup_retry.
A new standalone 'unavailable actuators' sensor. Rejected for entity bloat; categorized attributes on the existing sensor carry the same signal.

Building D2 reconcile straight away. Rejected in favor of study-first; the study materially changed the design (live-intent-only, no snapshots — because devices self-default on power-up and RestoreEntity can't help).

Unit-mirror test for the D1 sensor (copy the logic into the test). Rejected as the weak pattern prior cycles flagged; used the live house as the behavioral oracle instead (known-offline actuators existed at deploy time) + suite-baseline gate.
implications: A durable separation emerged mirroring entry 025's 'automation vs safety bound': INPUT failures degrade detection, ACTUATOR failures degrade actuation — they need different visibility and different recovery. The old tracker conflated 'unavailable entities' with 'unavailable inputs' and so missed half the failure surface.

The live house beat the unit harness as a validation oracle for this class: the AV Shelly re-dropping post-restart gave a real offline_since_restart observation no mock would have staged, and stair-closet recovering proved the clearing path. For diagnostic sensors over real device state, prefer live acceptance criteria over logic-mirror tests.
Reload-as-recovery is mostly a placebo for the common failure mode (device off-WiFi). The evidence is now recorded; future 'just reload it' impulses should re-read this entry.
The operator's escalating design taste held across all three deliverables: richer-not-basic (D1), study-before-build (D2), safety-pattern-or-discard (D3). Match proposals to that bar up front.
AV-closet Shelly1PMGen3 is genuinely flaky hardware (2 offline episodes in one day) — operator-side fix pending; URA now surfaces it instead of silently failing.
follow_up: v5.7.2 CLOSED (L1-L4 PASS, README write-back committed). AV Shelly hardware/WiFi check = operator-side.
D2 build = its own Tier 2-DB cycle when operator green-lights (plan: docs/planning/PLANNING_reconcile_on_return.md, delivered to operator).

v5.7.1 migration L3 FAIL still open (runtime banking-OFF not honored when legacy options key absent) — v5.7.2-candidate scope was superseded by this actuator cycle; now a small standalone fix: default-OFF approach per operator.
WS-B (guest HVAC actuation) still gated on WS-A L3 live observation (a real all-away day; watch veto_path).
Census over-count investigation (the REAL live guest-mode cause) still open; camera-census outdoor exclusion = docs-only per operator.
Inclement-weather reserve (task #17) still needs operator D0 (wire the Dynamic Weather NWS entity).
Jullison WiFi / Inovelli lights + the batch of off-WiFi Shelly/Sonoff devices = operator-side network follow-up.
ship_target: v5.6.0 + v5.6.1/.2/.3 + v5.7.0 + v5.7.1 + v5.7.2 ALL SHIPPED + LIVE-VALIDATED (v5.7.2 closed 2026-07-01 with L1-L4 PASS). D2 = design filed, not built. D3 = parked on OC plan Appendix C.
